question: What is Merrill's advisor growth strategy, and how has it changed?

claims.text: On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-14), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, and that results "reflect strong demand for advice, and our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (published 2026-07-14), Borthwick said the Merrill leaders are trying to "just keep growing the sales force," that the aim is 5% "over the course of the next 3 to 5 years" (the "Merrill 5% guide"), and that "adviser attrition is now at near historic lows."

On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-14), Borthwick said both Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform and our ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for clients."

On the 1Q26 call (published 2026-04-15), Borthwick said the firm is "driving productivity higher on both newer and existing members of our financial advisers team, and we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers."

On the 4Q25 call (published 2026-01-14), Borthwick said "we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy," and pointed to a training program for wealth management, Bank of America and Merrill as what the firm can "keep driving" to improve net new flows.

Merrill's Advisor Development Program recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes training as the entry route: it offers "industry leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses," base salary and "unlimited earning potential," and coaching and mentorship. It lists the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 licences, an approximately 13-month path that includes three months of licensing, and a Financial Advisor stage of approximately 1-4 years before progression to Merrill Core Advisor.

Merrill's recruiting page for experienced advisors (page content as of 2026-11-03) pitches "infrastructure that supports lead generation through Bank of America's global bank, trust division and strong market presence" and access to Merrill's wealth management platform and Bank of America's banking and trust capabilities.

Trade press (AdvisorHub, published 2026-11-16) reports that Merrill largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017. It says the firm returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. It adds that Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year.

On the 1Q25 call (published 2025-04-15), Borthwick said GWIM expense growth of 9% supported investment in technology and "the cost of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the private bank."

On the 2Q25 call (published 2025-07-16), Borthwick said the firm "continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors," and that approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors. He again cited the cost of hiring experienced advisors within expense growth.

On the 4Q25 call (published 2026-01-14), Borthwick described experienced-advisor recruiting as picking up but "not an enormous part of our strategy," alongside a training program. On the 1Q26 call (published 2026-04-15) he said the firm continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-14), Borthwick framed the goal as growing the sales force toward a 5% aim over 3 to 5 years, said the firm was "off to a good start," and said adviser attrition was "near historic lows."

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-09-11) says Merrill "ramps up advisor recruiting efforts," and reports several team wins in early September 2026. These include a $1.2 billion UBS team in Santa Fe, and advisors from Morgan Stanley, Truist and Wells Fargo with a combined $1.8 billion.
On the 2Q25 call (published 2025-07-16), Borthwick said approximately one-third of Q2 net new households were added by newly trained advisors, a result of the training program.

The 4Q25 earnings release (published 2026-01-14) reports about 18K net new households added by Merrill Wealth Management in FY25. The 3Q26 release (published 2026-10-14) reports about 4.2K net new $500K+ households in 3Q26.

Merrill Wealth Management revenue was $5,905 million in 3Q26, against $5,261 million in 3Q25 (GWIM supplement, published 2026-10-14). The firm cites advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools as expanding capacity (3Q26 call). It gives no per-advisor productivity figure in these chunks.
On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-14), management described advisor attrition only qualitatively, as "near historic lows."

Positioning the firm states: the 2025 investor day deck (published 2025-11-05) describes Merrill as the "second largest traditional wealth manager in the U.S." with a "leading advisor force." The 3Q26 release (published 2026-10-14) cites more than 300 Merrill advisors on Barron's 2026 Top 1,500 Financial Advisors and 24 on Financial Planning's 2026 Top 40 Brokers Under 40.

Where trade press says Merrill is winning advisors: AdvisorHub (published 2026-11-16) reports a $1 billion UBS private wealth team in Boston joining Merrill. It also reports Merrill adding an advisor managing $205 million from Morgan Stanley and one overseeing $150 million from Edward D. Jones & Co. WealthManagement.com (published 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-11) reports teams from Morgan Stanley, UBS, Truist and Wells Fargo.

Where trade press says Merrill is losing advisors: WealthManagement.com (published 2026-11-03) reports J.P. Morgan recruited Merrill advisor Tiffany Yu (about $940 million) and hired another Merrill alum as Southeast Regional Director. InvestmentNews (published 2026-10-14) reports an advisor taking about $580 million from Merrill to LPL's independence model. InvestmentNews (published 2026-11-12) reports a Merrill veteran moving to an independent RIA and describes a broader pattern of wirehouse advisors moving to independent practices.

adjacent.text: The 2025 investor day deck (published 2025-11-05) shows ">15K" wealth advisors for the combined Merrill | Private Bank unit.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: The Q4 2023 GWIM supplement (published 2024-01-12) shows total wealth advisors of 18,916 at period end, and its footnote says the figure includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's. This count also includes Consumer Banking advisors and is dated 2023.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-11), citing Wolfe Research data through Aug. 13, reports Bank of America had a net loss of 552 advisors, the largest among firms compared. Edward Jones and Equitable Advisors followed with 334 each.
adjacent.differs_because: Net advisor headcount change is not attrition: it nets hires against departures. It is also a Bank of America-level figure from trade press, which is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-09-08), citing Wolfe Research, reports Bank of America had a net loss of 552 advisors through Aug. 13, the largest among firms listed. LPL had the highest net gain at 378 and Raymond James gained 293.
adjacent.differs_because: This is a Bank of America-level net headcount figure from trade press, which is indicative, not authoritative. It does not isolate Merrill and is not attrition.

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America annual or quarterly supplement or investor-day disclosure giving Merrill-only financial advisor headcount

gaps.what: Merrill does not disclose advisor attrition as a number, or a count of experienced-advisor hires or trainee graduates. Management has described attrition only qualitatively as "near historic lows."
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America earnings call Q&A, investor-day materials, or Merrill management disclosures giving advisor attrition and hiring counts

gaps.what: No per-advisor productivity metric (revenue or assets per advisor) for Merrill appears in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America investor-day materials or Merrill management disclosures giving revenue or assets per advisor

gaps.what: Merrill's explicit retention programs (for example deferred compensation or team support) are not described in the evidence; the only retention evidence is the qualitative attrition comment.
gaps.suggested_source: Merrill advisor recruiting or compensation materials, or an investor-day presentation on advisor retention

gaps.what: The firm's own filings, calls and decks in the evidence do not name the competitors it recruits against or is losing advisors to. The competitor names above come only from trade press, which is indicative, not authoritative.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America investor-day Q&A or management interviews naming competitive recruiting dynamics; FINRA BrokerCheck or Wolfe Research advisor-movement data
